pairs.evidence: packages/kernel/src/job-queue-core.ts:78 The worker counts store rows in `running` against lane capacity on every look, but its only staleness sweep (`recover`) runs once at loop start and the per-slot orphan sweep runs only inside a claim. A job left `running` by a dead process outside the worker (a CLI or a route drive) fills a capacity-1 lane (gpu.local, box.render), so no claim is ever attempted and the ghost is never swept until the worker restarts: there is no upper bound on how long a dead job can pose as a working one.

techniques.evidence: packages/kernel/src/job-queue-core.ts:78 Tier one (heartbeat, step events) exists. Tier two runs only at startup and on a claim, never periodically, so a ghost `running` row on a full lane blocks the pick that would have swept it.
packages/kernel/src/job-core.ts:212 Every job transition goes through one door against the closed jobMachine table. The holder carries a bootId, so a reused pid counts as a different incarnation.
packages/kernel/src/job-worker.ts:84 The SQLite store is authoritative and transitions commit in transactions. Recovery reconciles `running` claims before the loop admits anything.

packages/kernel/src/job-run.ts:212 Liveness is a renewable lease with its own renewal timer at TTL/3, and every booking tx presents its fence (assertFence, line 324). That is the lease rung the technique says to stop at.

packages/kernel/src/lease.ts:285 Narrow case. The same-host pid probe has two values: any probe error other than EPERM reads as dead (`gone`), not unknown. Foreign-host holders are correctly left to TTL.

packages/kernel/src/job-run.ts:172 The slot cap is enforced at the one claim door as per-slot leases. A run total (ceilingUsd frozen at enqueue) is checked before each step in job-core next(). The supervisory third number is not in this context.
packages/kernel/src/job-run.ts:248 A yield parks the job with its outputs kept and releases the slot. The next drive claims under the same job id with a new fence.
packages/kernel/src/job-core.ts:192 Done is derived from booked outputs (the plan's missing steps), not from a producer's claim. An ending is done/failed/interrupted/stopped, never folded.
packages/kernel/src/job-worker.ts:71 Executors are co-located and read one shared store. The technique calls the outbound discipline ceremony in this case.
